items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I would listen to Mahalia Jackson or I would listen to The Five Satins

ctx.x: Plus you could stand in the store and read the backs of them.

Oh man, I mean see, when I was a kid I used to allow myself one mono record a week, because I was working in high school to save money to go to college, right? So when I got my paycheck on Friday I would go to a record store in Upper Darby which was the town next to the town I lived in, Yeadon, which is right outside of Philly, Riles Record Store, and then I would, for my $1.98 mono record, I’d look at five thousand records before I made my choice. What was it going to be? And there was something about that that…

there and you’d find out a new record came out you weren’t aware of, and they would play them for me. The guy and his wife that owned that store were so nice to me. They would play it. And there used to be a place in South Philly called Paramount Record Shop, it was one of the few black owned record shops in the city, a guy named Felix owned it. And I would come in on a Saturday afternoon and they’d say oh here comes the white boy again. And I’d listen. And I’d say well can you play me — so finally they just like…
